title: Intent to Destroy
thesis: The Government of Canada knowingly expanded MAID via Bill C-7 (2021), removing the 'reasonably foreseeable death' safeguard and inviting persons whose suffering is socioeconomic in origin into a state-administered death program. Rome Statute Article 6(a) forbids killing members of an identifiable group with intent to destroy that group in whole or in part.

scenes.headline: Intent to Destroy
scenes.subhead: Bill C-7 stripped the safeguard that distinguished assisted dying from social engineering.

scenes.speaker: Hon. David Lametti, Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
scenes.speaker_meta: House of Commons Hansard, 2nd Reading of Bill C-7, 2020-10-19
scenes.quote: Bill C-7 expands eligibility for medical assistance in dying by removing the requirement that a person's natural death be reasonably foreseeable.

scenes.context: Track 2 MAID is created. A person whose death is NOT reasonably foreseeable can now be killed by a clinician under federal law. The Senate amendment further opens eligibility to those whose sole underlying condition is mental illness (sunset 2024 → deferred to 2027).

5.1% of all deaths in Canada were administered by the state through MAID in 2024 — the fifth consecutive year of double-digit growth since C-7 took effect. Health Canada Fifth Annual Report on Medical Assistance in Dying.
Track 2 is the cohort whose death was NOT reasonably foreseeable. Approximately 776 Canadians were killed in 2024 under the C-7 expansion that the 2016 framework explicitly excluded.

scenes.headline: Why this satisfies Article 6(a)
scenes.body:
Rome Statute Article 6(a) requires (i) killing of members of an identifiable group, and (ii) intent to destroy that group in whole or in part. C-7 was not an accident. It was debated, amended, and passed with explicit awareness — recorded in Hansard — that removing the foreseeable-death safeguard would route disabled, chronically ill, and economically vulnerable Canadians into a state-administered death program.

The group is identifiable: persons with disabilities, persons with chronic illness, and persons whose suffering is socioeconomic in origin. The killing is documented. The intent is on the parliamentary record.
